extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent applicants/attorneys (practitioners involved in prosecution)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining, documenting, and litigating restriction requirements in patent applications — when inventions are distinct/independent/unrelated, how to establish examiner burden, linking/rejoinder, elections of species, and related procedural notices (Ochiai/Brouwer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcombination distinctness (combination/subcombination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each subcombination is distinct from the combination as claimed if: (A) the combination does not require the particulars of the subcombination as claimed for patentability (e.g., to show novelty and unobviousness), and (B) the subcombination can be shown to have utility either by itself or in another materially different combination. See MPEP § 806.05(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restriction between a combination and its subcombinations requires two-way distinctness and reasons for insisting on restriction. Examiner should point out why subcombination has separate utility and why the combination does not require the particulars of the subcombination. Use form paragraphs such as 8.16 and 8.15 as appropriate. If claims to multiple subcombinations are present, the presence of one can be evidence that details of another are not required (example: ABC/B/C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Serious burden requirement for restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction is only proper when there would be a serious burden if restriction were not required, as evidenced by separate classification, status, or field of search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must explain why a serious burden would exist if restriction is not required (see MPEP § 803 and § 808.02). Evidence can include separate classification, separate status in the art, or a different field of search. Mere conclusion is inadequate; give appropriate explanation/examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of multiple subcombination claims as evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Where claims to two or more subcombinations are presented along with a claim to a combination that includes the particulars of at least two subcombinations, the presence of a claim to the second subcombination is evidence that the details of the first subcombination are not required for patentability (and vice versa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete claim-set examples (e.g., ABC/B/C) to show that particulars of a subcombination are not required for patentability of the combination. This supports restricting subcombinations from each other and from the combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration and rejoinder when elected claims become allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon determining that all claims directed to an elected combination invention are allowable, the examiner must reconsider the propriety of the restriction requirement; if the combination is allowable in view of patentability of at least one subcombination, the restriction between the elected combination and patentable subcombination(s) will be withdrawn and allowable subcombinations that were searched must be rejoined. If a subcombination is elected and determined allowable, nonelected claims requiring all the limitations of the allowable claim will be rejoined (see MPEP § 821.04).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When allowable linking/ elected claims appear, withdraw restriction and rejoin dependent/non-elected claims that require all limitations. Follow rejoinder practice in MPEP § 821.04 and use the appropriate form paragraphs (e.g., 8.21.xx).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcombinations usable together — distinctness standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Subcombinations disclosed as usable together in a single combination are distinct if they do not overlap in scope and are not obvious variants, and if it is shown that at least one subcombination is separately usable (MPEP § 806.05(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 8.16 for restriction requirements between subcombinations usable together. Examiner should suggest a utility for the subcombination other than use with the other subcombination in bracketed example text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic claims and species interplay in restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Where subcombinations (or species) are species under a claimed genus and related, restriction must be determined by both election-of-species practice and related-inventions practice; if restriction is improper under either practice, it should not be required (MPEP § 806.04(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully assess generic claims: restriction generally cannot be required when only generic claims are presented unless the generic claim encompasses so many species that an unduly extensive search would be necessary. If species claims and generic claims co-exist, election of species may be required prior to search on merits in some situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden-shifting on examiner to document viable alternative use
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant proves or provides an argument, supported by facts, that the other use suggested by the examiner cannot be accomplished or is not reasonable, the burden is on the examiner to document a viable alternative use or withdraw the restriction requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant’s factual traversal forces the examiner to either supply another workable example of distinctness/use or drop the restriction. Examiner examples need not be documented but must be reasonably persuasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process vs apparatus distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: A process and apparatus for its practice can be shown to be distinct inventions if (A) the process as claimed can be practiced by another materially different apparatus or by hand; or (B) the apparatus as claimed can be used to practice another materially different process (MPEP § 806.05(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 8.17 may be used. Examiner must provide reasonable examples showing material differences; examples need not be documented. A process is 'practiced by hand' if it can be performed without using any apparatus. If applicant convincingly traverses, examiner must document another materially different process/apparatus or withdraw requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process of making vs product made distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: A process of making and a product made by the process are distinct if (A) the process as claimed is not an obvious process of making the product and the process can be used to make another materially different product; or (B) the product as claimed can be made by another materially different process (MPEP § 806.05(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations of different processes or products need not be documented initially. A product defined by the process of making it is still a product claim and can be restricted from the process if the examiner shows the product can be made by a materially different process. If applicant traverses, burden shifts to the examiner to document a viable alternative or withdraw the requirement. Use form paragraphs 8.18 and 8.21.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of potential rejoinder in Ochiai/Brouwer situations
rubrics_metrics.description: When restriction is required between product and process claims, if applicant elects product claims and product claims are later found allowable, withdrawn process claims that depend from or otherwise require all the limitations of the allowable product claim will be considered for rejoinder; rejoined process claims must meet all requirements of 35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103 and 112 (MPEP § 821.04(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must include form paragraph 8.21.04 in such restriction requirements. Applicant is advised to amend process claims during prosecution to require the limitations of the product claims to retain the right to rejoinder; failure may result in loss of rejoinder. Note: the prohibition against double patenting rejections under 35 U.S.C. 121 does not apply where restriction is withdrawn by examiner before patent issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apparatus vs product made distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: An apparatus and a product made by the apparatus are distinct if (A) the apparatus as claimed is not an obvious apparatus for making the product and the apparatus can be used to make another materially different product; or (B) the product as claimed can be made by another materially different apparatus (MPEP § 806.05(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 8.19 may be used. Examiner must show by way of example either (A) or (B); the example need not be documented. If applicant disproves the example, the examiner must suggest another viable example or withdraw the restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product vs process of using distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: A product and a process of using the product are distinct if (A) the process of using as claimed can be practiced with another materially different product; or (B) the product as claimed can be used in a materially different process (MPEP § 806.05(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must provide an example (not necessarily documented); if applicant shows the suggested alternative use cannot be accomplished, examiner must support another viable alternative or withdraw requirement. Use form paragraphs 8.20 and 8.21.04 where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-way relationship: product, process of making, process of using
rubrics_metrics.description: Where claims to product, process of making, and process of using are included in one application, a three-way restriction can only be made where the process of making is distinct from the product; if process of making and product are not distinct, process of using may be joined with product and process of making even though distinctness between product and process of using can be shown (MPEP § 806.05(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims include product and a process specially adapted for making the product and also a process of using, applicant may be required to elect either (A) the product and process of making it, or (B) the process of using. If the examiner cannot make a showing of distinctness between process of using and product, restriction cannot be required. Use form paragraph 8.20 where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related products/processes distinctness (three-part test)
rubrics_metrics.description: For related product inventions or related process inventions, inventions are distinct if (A) the inventions as claimed do not overlap in scope (mutually exclusive); (B) the inventions are not obvious variants; and (C) the inventions are either not capable of use together or can have a materially different design, mode of operation, function, or effect (MPEP § 806.05(j)). Two-way distinctness and reasons for insisting on restriction are necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Burden on examiner to provide an example; if applicant shows examiner's example not workable examiner must suggest another or withdraw restriction. Use form paragraphs 8.14.01 and 8.16 depending on relationship. See MPEP § 802.01 for relatedness guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermediate-final product distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: An intermediate product and a final product are distinct inventions if the intermediate and final products are mutually exclusive (not overlapping in scope), are not obvious variants, and the intermediate product as claimed is useful to make other than the final product (MPEP § 806.05(j)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 8.14 for intermediate-final product restriction requirements; conclude restriction basis with one of form paragraphs 8.21.01–8.21.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent inventions — definition and restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions as claimed are independent if there is no disclosed relationship between the inventions (they are unconnected in design, operation, and effect). If independent and there would be a serious burden on the examiner if restriction is not required, applicant should be required to restrict claims to one of such independent inventions (MPEP § 806.06).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: unrelated combination inventions with different modes/functions (apparel vs locomotive bearing), or a process and an apparatus that cannot practice the process. Use form paragraphs 8.20.02 (unrelated inventions) or 8.20.03 (unrelated product & process). Examiner must show reasons for serious burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unrelated inventions criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions are unrelated if they are not disclosed as capable of use together and they have different designs, modes of operation, and effects (MPEP § 806.06, form paragraph 8.20.02). For product/process, unrelated if the product cannot be used in or made by the process (form paragraph 8.20.03).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs 8.20.02 or 8.20.03 followed by one of form paragraphs 8.21.01–8.21.03. Insert reasons in bracketed text explaining unrelatedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination reasons required for insisting on restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Every requirement to restrict must include: (A) the reasons (not mere conclusion) why each invention as claimed is independent or distinct from the other(s); and (B) the reasons why there would be a serious burden on the examiner if restriction is not required (MPEP § 808).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons must be concise and specific. For combination/subcombination relationships point out why subcombination has separate utility and why combination does not require particulars. Where a disclosed relationship between species exists, discuss it and explain why it does not prevent restriction. Mere conclusory statements are inadequate. Use appropriate form paragraphs (8.01, 8.02, 8.14–8.20.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of species — when required and how handled
rubrics_metrics.description: When restriction between species is appropriate, the examiner should send a restriction requirement or place a telephone requirement to restrict. Identify generic claims or indicate none are present (MPEP § 809.02(a)). Election of species may be required prior to a search in applications with multiple species and no generic claims or with species plus generic claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Election of species should not be required between species clearly unpatentable over each other; group together species considered clearly unpatentable over each other. If only generic claims are presented, restriction cannot be required unless the generic recites/encompasses a multiplicity of species making search unduly extensive. If applicant later presents species claims after an office action on generic claims, the Office may require election.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing examiner burden — three showing options
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish reasons for insisting on restriction, the examiner must show by appropriate explanation one of: (A) separate classification thereof; (B) a separate status in the art when classifiable together; or (C) a different field of search (MPEP § 808.02).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate classification shows recognition as a separate subject for inventive effort. Separate status may be shown by patents evidencing separate inventive effort/status. Different field of search exists where searching for one invention is unlikely to find art pertinent to the other (different classes/subclasses, electronic resources, search queries). Patents need not be cited to show classification/field differences. If classification and field of search are the same and no indication of separate future classification/field exists, no reasons for dividing exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking claims and their effect on restriction/rejoinder
rubrics_metrics.description: Linking claims (e.g., genus claims linking species or subcombination claims linking combinations) may prevent restriction if allowable; linking claims and the inventions they link are examined with the elected invention. When all claims directed to the elected invention are allowable, if any linking claim is allowable the restriction must be withdrawn and non-elected claims depending from or requiring all limitations of the linking claim must be rejoined and examined (MPEP § 809).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If restriction was predicated on nonallowability of linking claims, applicant may retain non-elected claims in the application. If canceled nonelected claims exist, upon allowance of linking claims the examiner must notify applicant that canceled claims depending on the allowable linking claim may be reinstated and will be examined. See MPEP § 821.04 for rejoinder practice.
